# Introduction

This vignette uses empirical area-unit data for Auckland, New Zealand. The data
are included as external package files so the examples can be run after the
package is installed.

```{r setup}
devtools::load_all()
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Load the Auckland Data

Files in `inst/extdata` are installed with the package. Use `system.file()` to
find them.

```{r data-paths}
auck_dir <- system.file("extdata", "auck", package = "seg")

if (auck_dir == "") {
  auck_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "auck")
}

auck_shp <- file.path(auck_dir, "auck.shp")
auck_pop <- file.path(auck_dir, "auck_pop.csv")

file.exists(auck_shp)
file.exists(auck_pop)
```

Read the shapefile with `sf`. The shapefile contains counts for Korean
residents and total population in 1991, 1996, 2001, and 2006.

```{r read-data}
auck <- sf::st_read(auck_shp, quiet = TRUE)
pop <- read.csv(auck_pop)

nrow(auck)
names(auck)
head(pop[, c("au_no", "au_name", "kr06", "pop06")])
```

For the examples below, define two mutually exclusive groups: Korean residents
and all other residents in 2006.

```{r groups}
auck$Korean <- auck$KR06
auck$Non_Korean <- auck$POP06 - auck$KR06
auck$korean_share <- auck$Korean / auck$POP06

summary(auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean", "korean_share")])
```

# Plot Raw Population Data

The raw map shows the share of residents identified as Korean in each area
unit.

```{r raw-map}
ggplot(auck) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = korean_share), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x, 1), "%")) +
  labs(fill = "Korean share") +
  theme_minimal()
```


# Calculate local environments and segregation indices.

`spseg()` produces both local environment data for specified bands as well as segregation indices based on those local environments. You can return the environments, the indices, or both. Here we specify `output='full'` to get both the indices and the local environments back. `search='kdtree'`, `neighbors='radius'`, and `measures='all'` are specified explicitly as well, but these are also the defaults. 

```{r first-run}
auck_poly_seg <- spseg(
  auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean")],
  bands=c(1,2000,5000),
  search="kdtree",
  neighbors="radius",
  measures="all",
  output="full"
)
```

And we can view the indices in  a `data.frame`

```{r}
(auck_poly_ind<-as.data.frame(auck_poly_seg,what="indices"))
```


# Plot Local Environment Data

`as.data.frame()` methods are available. Specifying `what='env'` and `shape='long'` returns the local environments in a tidy data.frame. 

```{r localenv-map}
auck_poly_env<-as.data.frame(auck_poly_seg,what="env",shape="long") 
auck_poly_env$Total<-with(auck_poly_env, Korean+Non_Korean)
auck_poly_env$Korean_Share <- with(auck_poly_env,Korean/Total)

ggplot(auck_poly_env) + 
  geom_sf(aes(geometry=geometry,fill = Korean_Share+0.001), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x, 1), "%"), transform='log10') +
  facet_wrap(vars(band),ncol=3,
             labeller=as_labeller(
               function(x) paste('Bandwidth =',x,'m'))) +
  labs(fill = "Spatially\nWeighted\nKorean share\n(log scale)") +
  theme_void()
```

# Population Surfaces

The default `surface="raw"` uses the area-unit data directly. For areal data, it is sometimes useful to first redistribute the counts to a grid. The `surface="grid"` option spreads the population in each polygon evenly over square-grid points before the local environments are calculated.

```{r grid-surface}
auck_grid_seg <- spseg(
  auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean")],
  surface = "grid",
  surface_geometry = 'polygons',
  cellsize = 200,
  bands = c(1, 2000, 5000),
  output = "full"
)
```

The same `spseg()` call also produces segregation indices and local environments from the grid-based population surface.

```{r grid-surface-indices}
(auck_grid_ind<-as.data.frame(auck_grid_seg, what = "indices"))

auck_grid_env<-as.data.frame(auck_grid_seg,what="env",shape="long") 
auck_grid_env$Total<-with(auck_grid_env, Korean+Non_Korean)
auck_grid_env$Korean_Share <- with(auck_grid_env,Korean/Total)
```

The `surface="pycno"` option also constructs a grid, then applies groupwise pycnophylactic interpolation. Each group is smoothed separately, then rescaled within each area unit after every iteration so the known group totals are preserved.

```{r pycno-surface}
auck_pycno_seg <- spseg(
  auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean")],
  surface = "pycno",
  surface_geometry = 'polygons',
  celldim = 200,
  bands = c(1,2000, 5000),
  output = "full"
)
```

The segregation indices and local environments can be extracted in the same way.

```{r pycno-surface-indices}
(auck_pycno_ind<-as.data.frame(auck_pycno_seg, what = "indices"))

auck_pycno_env<-as.data.frame(auck_pycno_seg,what="env",shape="long") 
auck_pycno_env$Total<-with(auck_pycno_env, Korean+Non_Korean)
auck_pycno_env$Korean_Share <- with(auck_pycno_env,Korean/Total)
```

We can view all of the local environments based on the two approaches

```{r pycno-surface-localenv}
auck_poly_env$surface<-'polygon'
auck_grid_env$surface<-'grid'
auck_pycno_env$surface<-'pycnophylactic'
auck_env <- rbind(auck_poly_env,auck_grid_env,auck_pycno_env)

auck_env$Total <- with(auck_env, Korean + Non_Korean)
auck_env$Korean_Share <- with(auck_env, Korean / Total)

auck_env[auck_env$surface!='polygon',] |> 
ggplot(aes(geometry = geometry, 
              fill = Korean_Share+0.001,
              alpha=log(Total+1))) +
  geom_sf(color=NA,linewidth=0) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x, 1), "%"),
    na.value = "grey90",transform="log"
  ) +
  facet_grid(rows=vars(surface),cols=vars(band),switch="y") +
  labs(fill = "local share") +
  theme_void()+
  guides(color='none',alpha='none')
```

And we can plot the segregation indices across bandwidths for all three approaches

```{r}
auck_poly_ind$surface<-'polygon'
auck_grid_ind$surface<-'grid'
auck_pycno_ind$surface<-'pycnophylactic'
auck_ind<-rbind(auck_poly_ind,auck_grid_ind,auck_pycno_ind)

ggplot(auck_ind, aes(x=band,y=value,color=surface)) +
  geom_line() + theme_minimal() + facet_wrap(~measure,nrow=1) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)

```

# Bandwidth Sensitivity

Spatial segregation measures can change with the geographic scale used to
construct local environments. When we calculated the segregation measures, we already specified only three bandwidths. We could use more bandwidths, here just using the original polygons. 

```{r}
powers<-3:5
incr<-seq(0.2,1,by=0.1)
bws<-c(1, 1000, 1500, seq(2000,20000,by=1000))

auck_seg_bw <- spseg(
  auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean")],
  bands=bws,
  surface='raw',
  weighting='biweight',
  power=3,
  search = "kdtree",
  neighbors = "radius",
  measures = "all",
  output = "full"
)
```

We can extract the corresponding segregation measures using `as.data.frame()` with `what='indices'`. If we want the data in a tidy long format data frame, we can further specify `shape='long'`.

```{r bandwidth-sequence}
head(auck_ind_bw<-as.data.frame(auck_seg_bw ,what="indices",shape="long"))
```

Then we can plot the resulting segregation curves:

```{r bandwidth-curve-biweight}
auck_ind_bw |> 
ggplot(aes(x = band, y = value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Bandwidth (m)", y = "Measure value") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

The default uses biweights. We can also try the unweighted approach:

```{r bandwidth-curve-unweighted}
spseg(
  auck[, c("Korean", "Non_Korean")],
  bands = bws,
  weighting='unweighted',
  neighbors = "radius",
  measures = "all",
  output = "full"
) |>
  as.data.frame(what = 'indices', shape = 'long') |>
  ggplot(aes(x = band, y = value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap( ~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Bandwidth (m)", y = "Measure value") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```


The exposure/isolation values are a bit more complited, but can be returned in long form using the `what='exposure'` option in `as.data.frame()`.

```{r exposure-curve}
head(auck_poly_exp<-as.data.frame(auck_seg_bw, what = "exposure") )

auck_poly_exp |> 
ggplot(aes(x = band, y = exposure,color=from_group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=function(x) { format(100*x,digits=2) }) +
  facet_wrap(~ to_group, scales = "free_y",
             labeller=as_labeller(
               function(x) { paste("%",x) })) +
  labs(x = "Bandwidth (m)", y = "%",color='focal group') +
  theme_minimal()
```
